import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.model_selection import StratifiedKFold
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Check if any feature shows significant association with outcome
    p_values = []
    for fid in feats.ids:
        col = feats.column(fid)
        x = feats.x[:, col]
        t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(x[feats.y==1], x[feats.y==0], equal_var=False)
        p_values.append(p_val)
    
    # If no feature is significantly associated, return empty design
    if all(p > 0.05 for p in p_values):
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Use stratified CV to check for robust associations
    skf = StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42)
    valid_features = []
    
    for train_idx, test_idx in skf.split(feats.x, feats.y):
        x_train, y_train = feats.x[train_idx], feats.y[train_idx]
        x_test, y_test = feats.x[test_idx], feats.y[test_idx]
        
        # For each feature, fit logistic regression and check AUC
        for fid in feats.ids:
            col = feats.column(fid)
            lr = LogisticRegression(random_state=42, max_iter=1000)
            lr.fit(x_train[:, col].reshape(-1, 1), y_train)
            pred = lr.predict_proba(x_test[:, col].reshape(-1, 1))[:, 1]
            auc = roc_auc_score(y_test, pred)
            
            if auc > 0.55:  # Minimum threshold for inclusion
                valid_features.append(fid)
                break  # Only need one fold to validate
    
    # Remove near-duplicates based on correlation
    unique_features = []
    for fid in valid_features:
        is_duplicate = False
        for uf in unique_features:
            if abs(np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, feats.column(fid)], 
                              feats.x[:, feats.column(uf)])[0,1]) > 0.6:
                is_duplicate = True
                break
        if not is_duplicate:
            unique_features.append(fid)
    
    # Return best features as drivers if they exist
    if len(unique_features) > 0:
        # Select top features by t-statistic
        t_stats = []
        for fid in unique_features:
            col = feats.column(fid)
            x = feats.x[:, col]
            t_stat, _ = stats.ttest_ind(x[feats.y==1], x[feats.y==0], equal_var=False)
            t_stats.append(abs(t_stat))
        
        sorted_indices = np.argsort(t_stats)[::-1][:MAX_DRIVERS]
        drivers = tuple(unique_features[i] for i in sorted_indices)
        
        # Include all features that passed validation in columns
        columns = tuple(unique_features)
        
        # Simple interaction term approach: look for strong correlations
        products = []
        for i, fid1 in enumerate(columns):
            for j, fid2 in enumerate(columns[i+1:], i+1):
                corr = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, feats.column(fid1)], 
                                  feats.x[:, feats.column(fid2)])[0,1]
                if abs(corr) >= 0.6:
                    products.append((fid1, fid2))
        
        # Weighted score using top features
        loadings = {}
        for i, fid in enumerate(drivers):
            col = feats.column(fid)
            x = feats.x[:, col]
            t_stat, _ = stats.ttest_ind(x[feats.y==1], x[feats.y==0], equal_var=False)
            loadings[fid] = t_stat
        
        return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=products, loadings=loadings)
    
    return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
